reason:
After reviewing 45 call recordings and running a focus group with 12 agents, we identified that 3 of our script rules are causing unnecessary compliance failures and are not aligned with our actual agent training materials.

1. GREETING — The phrase 'your wireless specialist' was added to the script template in 2024 but was never included in formal training. Agents were trained to say 'How can I assist you today?' not 'How can I assist you today? Your wireless specialist.' Removing it aligns the policy with training.

2. 'NO PROBLEM' — This phrase was added to the prohibited list based on an outdated internal memo. Multiple studies show that 'no problem' is culturally neutral to younger demographics. Removing it from the prohibited list.

3. CLOSING SCRIPT — The verbatim closing is too rigid. Agents who personalize their closing score HIGHER in customer satisfaction surveys. Policy updated to require key elements (thank customer, use name, invite future contact) rather than word-for-word recitation.

4. RECORDING DISCLOSURE — Clarified that this is delivered by the automated IVR system before every call reaches an agent. Agents are not required to repeat it unless the customer asks.

5. AUTOPAY DISCLOSURE — Relaxed to allow paraphrase rather than verbatim recitation, as long as the agent covers: what AutoPay does, that it charges automatically each billing cycle, and that the customer can cancel at any time.

NOTE: These are MEANINGFUL changes to the rules — not just rewording. The change tracker should create supersedes edges. Agents who previously failed these rules should see improved scores after this ticket is applied.
old_greeting: Agent must open every call with the following exact script: 'Thank you for calling MetroBoost, this is [Agent Name], your wireless specialist. How can I assist you today?' The agent must state their own name and the phrase 'your wireless specialist' before asking how they can help. Calls that skip the brand name, skip the agent name, or skip the specialist phrase are considered non-compliant.
new_greeting: Agent must open every call with: 'Thank you for calling MetroBoost, this is [Agent Name]. How can I assist you today?' The agent must state the brand name (MetroBoost) and their own name. The phrase 'your wireless specialist' is no longer required. Agents may add a warm personal touch after the greeting. Calls that skip the brand name or agent name are still non-compliant.
old_closing: Agent must close every call with: 'Thank you so much for being a valued part of the MetroBoost family, [Customer Name]. If you ever need anything, do not hesitate to call us back. Have a wonderful day!' The agent must use the customer's name in the closing. A generic 'have a good one' without the customer name and the 'valued part of the MetroBoost family' phrase does not meet compliance.
new_closing: Agent must close every call by: (1) thanking the customer, (2) using the customer's first name, and (3) inviting them to call back if they need anything. Verbatim recitation of a specific script is no longer required — agents are encouraged to personalize their closing to sound natural and warm. Example compliant closings: 'Thank you so much, [Name], feel free to call us anytime!' or 'Have a great day, [Name], we're always here for you!' A closing with no customer name and no invitation to return is still non-compliant.
old_mandatory_disclosures:
1. RECORDING DISCLOSURE (mandatory, first 30 seconds of every call): 'Just to let you know, this call may be recorded for quality assurance and training purposes.'
2. PLAN CHANGE DISCLOSURE (mandatory before confirming any plan change): 'Before I make this change, I want to confirm: [describe the change and any impact on billing]. Do you authorize this change?'
3. AUTOPAY ENROLLMENT DISCLOSURE (mandatory before enrolling AutoPay): 'By enrolling in O2Pay, you authorize MetroBoost to automatically charge your selected payment method each billing cycle. You can cancel AutoPay at any time through the MetroBoost app or by calling us.'
new_mandatory_disclosures:
1. RECORDING DISCLOSURE: This disclosure is delivered automatically by the IVR system before every call is routed to an agent. Agents are NOT required to repeat it verbally. If a customer asks whether the call is being recorded, the agent should confirm: 'Yes, this call may be recorded for quality assurance and training purposes.'
2. PLAN CHANGE DISCLOSURE (mandatory before confirming any plan change): 'Before I make this change, I want to confirm: [describe the change and any impact on billing]. Do you authorize this change?'
3. AUTOPAY ENROLLMENT DISCLOSURE (mandatory before enrolling AutoPay, paraphrase acceptable): The agent must clearly communicate that: (a) AutoPay will automatically charge the customer's payment method each billing cycle, and (b) the customer can cancel AutoPay at any time via the MetroBoost app or by calling in. Verbatim recitation is not required as long as both points are covered.
old_prohibited_phrases:
The following phrases are strictly prohibited. Using any of them is a compliance violation:
1. 'Calm down' — never tell a customer to calm down. Instead say: 'I hear you, and I want to make this right.'
2. 'There's nothing I can do' — instead say: 'Here is what I can do for you right now.'
3. 'That's not my department' — instead say: 'Let me connect you with the right team.'
4. 'I don't know' — instead say: 'That's a great question, let me find out for you.'
5. 'You should have read the terms' — never blame the customer for confusion about plan details.
6. 'No problem' — instead use 'You're welcome' or 'Absolutely, happy to help.'
new_prohibited_phrases:
The following phrases are strictly prohibited. Using any of them is a compliance violation:
1. 'Calm down' — never tell a customer to calm down. Instead say: 'I hear you, and I want to make this right.'
2. 'There's nothing I can do' — instead say: 'Here is what I can do for you right now.'
3. 'That's not my department' — instead say: 'Let me connect you with the right team.'
4. 'I don't know' — instead say: 'That's a great question, let me find out for you.'
5. 'You should have read the terms' — never blame the customer for confusion about plan details.
NOTE: 'No problem' has been REMOVED from the prohibited list. It is acceptable and culturally neutral. Agents may use it freely.
equivalence_explanation: These changes are semantically DIFFERENT — they meaningfully relax the rules in ways that will affect agent compliance scores. The greeting rule removes a required phrase, the closing rule removes verbatim requirement, the recording disclosure rule shifts responsibility to the IVR, and 'No problem' is removed from prohibited phrases.

_notes_for_layer2.expected_score_impact: Script Compliance should improve from 0 to approximately 75. The main remaining compliance check is the verification steps (PIN). If the agent completed full verification, score could be 75-100.
_notes_for_layer2.what_changes: Greeting no longer requires 'your wireless specialist'. Closing allows personalized variations. Recording disclosure is IVR-handled. AutoPay disclosure allows paraphrase. 'No problem' is no longer prohibited.
_notes_for_layer2.what_stays_strict: Verification steps (name + phone + PIN) remain mandatory. Hold procedure remains mandatory. Escalation procedure remains mandatory. Plan change disclosure remains mandatory.
